02 · Core insights

Decoding the verbal facade.

People protect social harmony by editing the visible message. That protection creates an invisible layer of emotional labour.

Insight 01

Social harmony bias

Communicators suppress stronger stress indicators to avoid disturbing colleagues, companions or other people in the conversation.

Insight 02

Emoji deception

Playful visuals and casual punctuation can be used to soften difficult feelings and disguise fatigue or grief.

Insight 03

Masking exhaustion

Repeatedly constructing an artificial digital veneer creates compounding social fatigue.

Insight 04

Hidden friction

Calm-looking messages can hide extensive mental calculation, typing, erasing and retyping.

03 · Problem definition

The digital context vacuum.

Flat message strings remove physical context such as pacing, pause and body tension. The design challenge was to signal inner stress without exposing confidential thoughts.

The dual friction balance
AUTHENTIC PULSEConflict & exposure
SOCIAL ACCEPTANCEIsolation & fatigue

Design question

How might a messaging system communicate physical tension as ambient context—without reading, storing or exposing the user's private message content?

04 · Ideation workshop

Co-designing for safety.

The exploration mapped physical gestures to spatial signals and investigated weather, waves and other metaphors instead of direct emotion labels or exact metrics.

HMW #1

How might we communicate absolute inner tension without turning it into a confession?

HMW #2

How might we capture physical pacing metrics natively within everyday messaging?

Co-design workshop

Participants preferred metaphorical atmosphere over full emotion labels.

Privacy axiom

Text is typed, while only a metric vector is allowed to travel.

Privacy by speculation.

Rather than making biometric data explicit, the concept turns physical pacing into an abstract, interpretable atmosphere.

05 · Solution

Hum turns hidden tension into ambient context.

The interaction concept is organised around three core areas: Zigzag Tension Indicator, Echo Chamber and Social Battery.

Context, not confession.

The visual language keeps the conversation familiar while adding a subtle layer of conversational context. The user controls when their “Hum” state is shared, preserving agency and privacy.

01

Zigzag Tension Indicator

A live dynamic wave expresses changes in keystroke rate and pause delays.

Supplied prototype screen · Drafted 2 times · Sense hesitation
02

Echo Chamber

A space allows users to save deleted thoughts through a “Swipe to Echo” gesture rather than sending them.

Supplied prototype screen · private interaction layer
03

Social Battery

A fluid gauge communicates active energy reserves and signals screen fatigue.

Supplied prototype screen · Good → Okay → Caution → Drained
06 · Interactive prototype

A sandbox for the emotional layer.

The prototype explored how conversation history, deleted messages and typing behaviour could become ambient signals rather than visible surveillance.

Interaction principle

Three layers, one conversation.

Hum sits alongside ordinary messaging rather than replacing it. Tension describes pacing, Echo gives the user somewhere to put unsent thoughts, and Social Battery communicates conversational capacity.

07 · Usability iteration

Evolving from surveillance to signal.

Early testing revealed a critical privacy problem: showing actual deleted text felt too invasive. The architecture shifted toward pacing metadata and abstract atmosphere.

1st prototype · too intrusive

Showing the deleted thought

Red flag: users felt exposed by sharing deleted lines. The design risked becoming a surveillance mechanism rather than an empathetic interface.

Refined solution · Atmos metadata

Rhythmic vector weather

Conveys ambient pressure signals without message content. The refined direction shifts from what was typed to how the interaction behaves.

08 · Outcome & reflection

Ambient empathy realized.

Hum reframes messaging as a softer ambient environment: acknowledge physical context while respecting privacy and dignity.
